subject: Recap: Inference economics discussion & pilot options
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Hana Sato <hana@quantumpay.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T16:18:00Z
Subject: Recap: Inference economics discussion & pilot options

Hana — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so you and your team have the same notes and next steps. I kept this focused on the economics levers we discussed and what a short pilot could look like.

Key pain points you shared:
- Production latency spikes impacting checkout flows during peak hours (90th pct latency target currently violated).
- Monthly inference spend has been trending up with user growth; finance wants a predictable unit cost and an internal ROI case.
- Strict data residency + audit requirements for transaction logs.

Goals you outlined:
- Reduce per-interaction inference cost by ~30% without degrading 90th pct latency beyond 150ms.
- Pilot within a constrained budget: your target is ~USD 15k/month for an initial committed window.
- Validate reliability under concurrent traffic (peak 120 rps sustained for 10m).

What we believe will move the needle (short summary):
1) Batching & request shaping: moving from synchronous single-request paths to a small continuous-batching window for non-time-critical flows — expected to reduce effective GPU time by ~20–30% for chat/generation workloads.
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt prefixes (checkout templates) — can cut tokens rendered by the model by ~15–35% depending on reuse.
3) Model sizing + quantization mix: recommend a 7B quantized variant for latency-sensitive endpoints and a 13B quantized for higher-quality background jobs; saves 25–40% vs full fp16 on equivalent throughput.
4) Smart routing & fallbacks: burst to cheaper regional variants during heavy load, with automatic rollback for quality regressions.

Quick back-of-envelope numbers (based on the forecast you shared in the call):
- Current monthly inference tokens (est): 120M prompt + 180M completion tokens = 300M tokens/mo.
- Baseline spend (current provider): ~USD 48k/mo (we used your sample rates).
- With levers above (conservative): expect 25–30% unit-cost reduction -> new spend ~USD 34–36k/mo.
- Pilot scenario (controlled scope): 6M tokens/mo focused on checkout flows -> pilot compute spend ~USD 1.8–2.5k/mo before reserved discounts.
- Committed pilot offer we typically start with: a 3-month reserved pilot, commit USD 12k/month (covers reservoir for burst, dedicated lanes for SLA) with a rollout path to steady-state.

Suggested next steps (timeline):
- R1 (by EOD Fri): I’ll send a tailored pilot pricing sheet + suggested config (attached as a PDF). Please share the CSV of weekly traffic distribution if possible (you mentioned finance could provide).
- R2 (next week): Solutions call (30–45m) with Soojin to map endpoints to batching/caching rules and pick test traffic slices.
- R3 (week after): Security design review with your security team; we’ll provide a short snapshot of audit/KMS options (we attached a short security-snapshot).

Open asks from your side:
- Final confirmation on the USD 15k/month budget ceiling for the pilot (you said you’d check).
- Provide a 2-week rolling sample of traffic/latency by endpoint (CSV is easiest).

Attachments included: quantumpay-traffic-forecast.csv (you shared), security-snapshot.pdf (Redwood summary), redwood-pilot-pricing-v1.pdf (pricing stub — draft).

If the budget line is firm at 15k, we can propose a 2-month reduced commitment option to fit that ceiling and focus on checkout flows only. Otherwise, the 3-month USD 12k/month reserved path gives better unit economics and a straighter path to production.

Happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

--

Attachment: security-snapshot.pdf (attached)

From: Hana Sato <hana@quantumpay.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: QuantumPay Finance <finance@quantumpay.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Inference economics discussion & pilot options

Rishi — thanks for the clear summary and for pulling numbers together. A few clarifications from our side after the call: 

1) Budget ceiling: finance confirmed we can do USD 15k/month but only for a short, explicit evaluation window (max 2 months) before we review for expansion.
2) Token counts: the CSV you referenced (I attached the one I pulled) is our mobile checkout + fraud check traffic; full-platform totals are higher but we want to scope the pilot narrowly.
3) Latency tolerance: for checkout we need p95 < 120ms ideally, p99 < 300ms. If batching increases p95 for checkout paths we need to ensure an always-on low-latency lane for critical calls.

Can you confirm: with a 2-month pilot at USD 15k/mo, can you guarantee a configuration that isolates checkout flows to stay within the latency targets while still delivering measurable cost savings elsewhere? Also please confirm if the pilot commitment includes any overage protection for burst days.

I've attached the traffic CSV you requested (quantumpay-traffic-forecast.csv). Security is already looped in on my side; they'll need the redwood security snapshot before we sign any pilot SOW.

Thanks — happy to schedule the Soojin session next week.

Best,
Hana Sato
Head of Product, QuantumPay
hana@quantumpay.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-19T22:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Recap: Inference economics discussion & pilot options

Hana — appreciated. Short answers below and an updated pilot option to match the 2-month USD 15k ceiling you confirmed.

Guarantees & isolation: yes — we can create an isolated low-latency lane for checkout (dedicated concurrency slices + warm KV cache) to keep p95 latency in the target range. That lane will be size-constrained and not batched; other background or non-critical calls will use a batched lane. We’ll instrument fallbacks so checkout never slows below the target.

Pilot commercial (two-month constrained pilot):
- Commitment: USD 15k/month for 2 months.
- Scope: checkout + fraud-checks (isolated low-latency lane) + one background endpoint group for batching/caching experiments.
- Deliverables: configuration & runbook, 2-week ramp plan, 14-day QA window, weekly syncs and a final ROI summary.
- Overage protection: we include 10% buffer for burst days; >10% will be billed at a predefined overage rate (see attached pricing PDF page 2).

Expected measurable outcomes by end of pilot:
- Checkout p95/p99 within SLA (we’ll instrument synthetic checks).
- 15–25% overall unit-cost reduction across tested endpoints (conservative estimate given your reuse patterns).
- Ops runbook so your infra team can reproduce rules for long-term rollouts.

Next steps:
1) I’ll update the pilot pricing PDF and SOW draft and send by EOD.
2) Soojin to set a technical session with your engineering team — proposed Tue/Thu next week (30–45m).
3) Security review: we’ll share expanded docs and a short architecture diagram for the VPC/KMS options.

If that matches what finance needs, we can prepare a short SOW for signature (DocuSign link) and schedule kick-off for the Monday after SOW execution.

I attached redwood-pilot-pricing-v1.pdf (updated) — highlights include the 2-month 15k path. Let me know if finance needs a PO or invoice-first approach.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
